rules: Values recorded only where read in an opened page or file. Every sourced value tagged QUESTIONABLE; computed values PROJECTION.
searched: Opened and read in full: 3M AF 163-2 datasheet (local copy, 21 pp, pdftotext) - source of all af163_cure rows.
Opened: Henkel EA 9394 AERO TPB Rev 7/2015 (datasheets.tdx.henkel.com) - rows recorded.
Opened: Henkel EA 9396.6MD AERO TDS Feb 2021 - rows recorded (potting grade).
Opened: 3M Scotch-Weld 2216 B/A Gray TDS Sep 2024 (multimedia.3m.com/mws/media/2366022O/) - rows recorded; no lap shear.
Opened: Hexcel HexBond 679 PDS (2025) and HexBond selector guide (2024 PDF) - rows recorded.
Opened: 3M AF 191 data sheet (multimedia.3m.com/mws/media/241227O/) - 275-400 F flexible cure (350 F typical); not a low-temperature film; nothing recorded.
Opened: Bristol repository abstract page for Adams and da Silva 2006 (JAST 20(15)) - rows recorded (abstract only).
Opened: JPL/NASA NESC slides 'Principles of Cryogenic Adhesive Bonding' (nescacademy.nasa.gov/downloadFile/1541) - rows recorded.
Opened: Porto MSc thesis (de Almeida 2005, 134 pp) - SFT experiment and cure-stage text recorded.
Opened: UMD dissertation (Kim 2023) - gel-point/effective cure shrinkage statement recorded.
Opened: AFIT thesis abstract page (Crooks 2003) - recorded; PDF 403.

Opened with no usable result: Nairn 'Residual stress effects in fracture of composites and adhesives' (6 pp; theory, no SFT value); Ashcroft et al. IJAA 2001 PDF (wrong paper for the query: DCB fracture); Korean thin-film epoxy residual-stress paper (Lee 2015, curvature method, no SFT value); PMC9739702 (Al/CFRP single-lap residual stress, no SFT number); PMC6073486 (phosphate adhesive); KAIST/KOASAS record of Lee and Lee 2008 (JS-only page).
Blocked (HTTP 403/406 or captcha): ScienceDirect, DTIC apps.dtic.mil, UBC open.library, CORE, Syensqo product pages, Elsevier linkinghub.

Web searches run: SFT/gel point/Tg bimaterial; EA 9394 TDS; AF 3109; FM 300-2; FM 94; EA 9658; Redux 609; 2216; da Silva and Adams; Jumbo 2010; FM 73M effective temperature drop; NASA bonded honeycomb thermal stress; relaxation of adhesive residual stress.

source.title: Analytical and Experimental Study on the Evolution of Residual Stresses in Composite Materials (MSc thesis)
source.org_or_authors: Jorge Borges de Almeida, Faculty of Engineering, University of Porto (supervisor P. M. P. R. C. Camanho)
source.location: Chapter 2, printed pp.8-9 (PDF p.33-34), Stage 2 and Stage 3
source.quote: Stage 2: This stage starts at the gel point of the resin. For epoxy resins, this happens for a degree of cure of about 0.6. ... From this point, the resin modulus begins to grow and the material picks up some stresses, which are quickly relieved because the temperature is relatively high comparing to Tg, being the material highly viscoelastic. Stage 3: The start of the resin's vitrification is the point at which Tg coincides with the cure temperature. From this point on until cool down to room temperature the stresses developed contribute greatly to the total amount of residual stress of the material.

rows.note: Gel (degree of cure about 0.6 for epoxy) is where stiffness appears, but stress is relaxed while T is well above Tg; lock-in is at vitrification (Tg rising to meet the cure temperature). No fraction relaxed is quantified. The thesis adds (Stringer et al.): 'most residual stress predictions are determined using Tg as the maximum cure reference temperature'.

source.title: Measurement of Effective Cure Shrinkage of Epoxy Molding Compound and Induced In-line Warpage During Molding Process (PhD dissertation)
source.org_or_authors: Changsu Kim (advisor Bongtae Han), University of Maryland
source.quote: The modulus is near zero when the polymer is uncured, but the modulus starts evolving after passing its gel point. Therefore, only the cure shrinkage accumulated after the gel point, known as the "effective cure shrinkage (ECS)", should be used to determine cure-induced residual stresses.

rows.note: Supports the gel-point rule for cure-shrinkage stress (not thermal-mismatch stress). Measured ECS of the EMC is 0.077 % (abstract) - a filled molding compound, not transferable to AF 163. Warpage began about 10 min after the start of the measurement ('effective gel point').

source.title: Principles of Cryogenic Adhesive Bonding (slides)
source.org_or_authors: Jim Denman (presented by Nataly Chen), JPL / California Institute of Technology, 353M Materials and Processes, Testing and Development
source.quote: Bonding and curing should occur under ambient conditions · Ambient cure minimizes thermal mismatch loads at the stress-free state · ... · UV Curing systems may provide a room temperature set point while allowing some elevated post-cure

rows.note: Supports bonding near the ambient/room end of the operating band; a cure at the 'mid-swing' of 271-302 K (about 286 K) is not discussed, and no source here says mid-swing is optimal. For a 271-302 K service band, ambient (about 293 K) is already inside the band.

rows.property: Measured thermal residual strain falls with lower cure temperature, repair bonds
rows.product: FM 73M film adhesive (cure temperatures not stated in abstract)
rows.condition: graphite/epoxy patch on 7075-T6 aluminium

source.title: Reduction of Thermal Residual Strains in Adhesively Bonded Composite Repairs (MSc thesis, AFIT-GAE-ENY-03-11J; abstract page only, full text blocked 403)
source.org_or_authors: Heather R. Crooks, Air Force Institute of Technology
source.quote: The hypothesis is that by reducing cure temperatures the CTE mismatch will be less dramatic thus yielding a more robust repair with a comparable fatigue crack growth rate.

rows.note: Only 7.4 % for EA 9696; a lower cure temperature is a first-order lever but the abstract does not give the temperature pair, so the sensitivity cannot be computed. Fatigue crack growth rate was not harmed by the lower cure.

rows.property: Low-temperature-cure film that avoids high-temperature thermal mismatch (80 C cure)
rows.condition: see rt_cure_adhesive

source.title: HexBond 679 Product Data Sheet (RTU-483-MC20)
source.quote: Cure cycle as low as 70°C for 8 hours (typically 4 hours @ 80°C)

rows.note: Lowest film-adhesive cure found that is also designed for honeycomb sandwich. Still 51 K above the top of the card's 302 K service band; not a 'mid-swing' cure.

gaps: No cure-at-mid-swing (cure near the middle of the operating temperature range) source was found; only the generic 'ambient cure minimises mismatch loads' slide from JPL (2026) and a lower-cure-temperature repair study (Crooks 2003, abstract only).

No measured fraction of thermal residual stress relaxed during cool-down, storage or service for AF 163, FM 73, FM 300, EA 9696 or any film-adhesive honeycomb bond was found. The Porto thesis says relaxation in CFRP laminates 'was impossible to quantify'. Value left null.

No stress-free temperature measured for AF 163-2U itself was found. The only numeric SFT in an opened source is the CFRP laminate figure in the Porto thesis (about 236 C vs 180 C cure), which the author calls inconclusive.

Adams and da Silva 2006 (SFT = cure temperature for a high-Tg adhesive, = Tg for a low-Tg adhesive in a mixed joint) was read from the Bristol abstract page only; full text is paywalled. The Jumbo, Ashcroft, Crocombe and Wahab 2010 paper (10.1016/j.ijadhadh.2010.03.009) was not opened (Elsevier blocked).

Lange, Toll, Manson and Hult (Polymer 1995 and 1997, bilayer-beam residual stress build-up above and below ultimate Tg) were identified in search results but ScienceDirect returned 403; the abstracts were not read, so nothing is recorded from them.
A UBC thesis (Albat) reported in a search snippet as measuring an effective stress-free temperature of 85.8 C for FM 73M was not opened (UBC and CORE pages blocked); that value is NOT recorded.
DTIC reports ADA394588, ADA222549, ADA231221 returned 403 and were not read.

Not opened (distributor snippets only, no values recorded): Syensqo/Cytec FM 300-2, FM 94, 3M AF 3109-2U/2K, Henkel EA 9658, EA 9309.3NA, standard EA 9396 AERO, Hexcel Redux 609 / HexBond 609 data sheets. Syensqo product pages returned 406. No FM 94 low-temperature cycle was confirmed.

Henkel EA 9394 bulletin has no honeycomb flatwise or drum-peel data; 3M 2216 B/A Gray TDS has no lap shear, Tg or flatwise value; HexBond 679 has no flatwise tensile value. 2216 data show only 7 days at 23 C and 2 h at 66 C cures.

AF 163-2U: no 2U-specific climbing-drum, vacuum-cure or lap-shear tables other than the MMM-A-132B/MIL-A-25463B rows; no beryllium-faced test data. All datasheet values are tests on aluminium skins and core. The datasheet states its data 'should not be used for specification purposes'.

3M datasheet CTE of 90e-6 /C is for the cured free film at -30 to 50 C and says the film is unsupported; the printed Tg method (DuPont 1090 DMA) does not say which DMA criterion (onset, E'' peak or tan delta) the 108 C refers to.
HexBond 679: 2025 data sheet and 2024 selector guide disagree (lap shear 29 vs 23 MPa; Tg 100 +/-5 vs 90 C; service -55 to 80 vs 65 C max). Both recorded.
EA 9396.6MD is a syntactic potting/edge-fill paste (density 0.63 g/ml), not a face/core bonding adhesive; recorded for its Tg-vs-cure data only.
